One in three developers say they've been laid off within the last two years
According to the State of the Industry survey, 34 percent of respondents have stated that they have been laid off in the last two years.
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
November 12, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
Image by tkmiller via Adobe Stock
In this year's
State of the Industry report
, an annual survey conducted by GDC Festival of Gaming, game industry professionals were asked to respond to questions concerning consistency of employment over the last two years—and some of the results are grim. One in three of those respondents, when asked if they have been laid off in the last 24 months, answered affirmatively,
indicating a sharp rise since the last report
. That marks 34 percent of pollees having been laid off, ballooning to 39 percent when limited just to answerers from the United States.
In the report, GDC notes that the survey results indicate a higher participation rate from people affected by layoffs, particularly in the United States.
The number of full-time employees in the United States has dropped from 59 percent last year to just 50 percent this year. At 21 percent, one-fifth report that they are currently unemployed, marking a striking 8-point increases from the previous year's 13 percent.

49 percent of respondents, rising to 55 percent in the US, reported that their companies have implemented some form of layoffs over the last year. The number seems to skew higher for those working at AAA studios, reaching 68 percent, while it decreases for workers at younger (14 percent) and older (35 percent) indie studios. Among these layoff plans, the top reasons cited were company restructuring, financial difficulties, and canceled projects.
Game workers were twice as likely to have been laid off in the past year (68 percent) than in the preceding year (32 percent). Of the respondents who said they were laid off once (79 percent), a smaller fraction reported being laid off twice (17 percent), and even less beyond that (3 percent). The largest sectors for layoffs were in quality assurance, marketing/PR, and visual and technical arts, while business operations and services were the least likely roles to face layoffs.
The churn is also slowly eroding consistency within the industry. For those that have found a new job after being laid off, only two-thirds (68 percent) are in a similar field. 28 percent of those respondents said their new job is similar to their previous one, 23 percent reporting that its better, and 17 percent stating that its worse.
9 percent state that they have left the industry altogether.
GameDeveloper.com and GDC Festival of Gaming are sibling organizations under Informa Festivals
Update 11/12:
This story has been updated to note additional context from the report concerning the representation of laid-off developers among survey respondents.
